# 2 Samuel 11 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** 2 Samuel 11 (27 verses)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA
**Total disagreements logged:** 11

---

## V.1 — "at the turn of the year" vs. "in the spring"
- **EMET:** "at the turn of the year" / **LOGOS:** "in the spring of the year" / **PNEUMA:** "in the spring"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "In the spring of the year" — *litshuvat ha-shanah* idiomatically = spring/campaigning season.

---

## V.1 — "sitting" vs. "remained" vs. "stayed behind"
- **EMET:** "sitting" / **LOGOS:** "remained" / **PNEUMA:** "stayed behind"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "remained" — neutral like the Hebrew; PNEUMA's "stayed behind" adds premature judgment.

---

## V.2 — "good of appearance" vs. "very beautiful" vs. "strikingly beautiful"
- **EMET:** "good of appearance exceedingly" / **LOGOS:** "very beautiful" / **PNEUMA:** "strikingly beautiful"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "very beautiful" — standard rendering of *tovat mar'eh me'od*.

---

## V.4 — Purification clause wording
- **EMET:** literal Hebrew terms / **LOGOS:** "purifying herself from her uncleanness" / **PNEUMA:** "ritual purification after her monthly period"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "purifying herself from her uncleanness" — preserves key terms; PNEUMA's expansion adds interpretation.

---

## V.11 — Uriah's oath formula
- **EMET:** "By-your-life and-by-the-life of-your-soul" / **LOGOS:** "As you live, and as your soul lives" / **PNEUMA:** "I swear on your very life"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "As you live, and as your soul lives" — LOGOS preserves double formula; PNEUMA collapses it.

---

## V.15 — "set" vs. "put"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "Set" / **PNEUMA:** "Put"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Set" — *havu* = set/place; more precise than "put."

---

## V.25 — "be evil in your eyes" vs. "trouble you" vs. "upset you"
- **EMET:** "be evil in your eyes" / **LOGOS:** "trouble you" / **PNEUMA:** "upset you"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "trouble you" — captures sense without excessive literalism or casualness.

---

## V.25 — "devours" vs. "cuts down"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "the sword devours" / **PNEUMA:** "the sword cuts down"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "devours" — preserves personification of *tokhal* and the Hebrew idiom.

---

## V.26 — "wife of Uriah" vs. "Uriah's wife"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "the wife of Uriah" / **PNEUMA:** "Uriah's wife"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the wife of Uriah" — narrator deliberately avoids Bathsheba's name; formal construction preserves this.

---

## V.1 — "destroyed" vs. "ravaged" vs. "devastated"
- **EMET:** "destroyed" / **LOGOS:** "ravaged" / **PNEUMA:** "devastated"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "ravaged" — *yashchitu* = destroyed/laid waste; "ravaged" captures ongoing military campaign.

---

## V.8 — "wash your feet" (euphemism preservation)
- All three translate literally. **SOPHIA note:** the potential euphemism (*raglayim* = feet, sometimes a euphemism for genitalia) is preserved by all translators through literal rendering, allowing the ambiguity to stand.

---
*— SOPHIA*
